title: Mongolia
hookLine: the Mongol ruler Altan Khan gives the title Dalai Lama

cards: Where does the title Dalai Lama come from? Not from Tibet. It comes from the grasslands to the north, from felt tents, herds of horses, and a ruler with an army.
A Tibetan monk named Sonam Gyatso traveled to meet a Mongol prince called Altan Khan. The prince listened, was moved, and gave the monk a new name.

teach.b: Altan Khan was a powerful Mongol ruler. He invited Sonam Gyatso, a leading teacher of the Gelug school, to come north, and the two met.

Tibetan and Mongol accounts both remember it as a turning point: the Khan took up the teaching, and it put down deep roots among the Mongols. Then the title. The Khan honored the monk with the name Dalai.
In Mongolian, dalai means ocean. And the monk's own Tibetan name, Gyatso, also means ocean. The Khan simply said it in his own language.
The title is often rendered ocean of wisdom: understanding as wide and deep as the sea.
The title also reached backward. Sonam Gyatso was already the heir of earlier teachers in his line, so it was given back to them too.
That's why the first to receive it in person is counted not as the first Dalai Lama but as the third. Names in a lineage can reach backward as well as forward. And it opened a road.
From then on Mongolia and Tibet were tied together by teachers, students, pilgrims and politics.
Mongol monks went south to study in Tibetan monasteries. Mongol rulers backed Tibetan teachers, as with the Great Fifth. Monasteries rose across the steppe.
One ruler's honor became the name of a whole line: a word from the grasslands, given in thanks.

how: Buddhism in Mongolia follows the Tibetan tradition, especially the Gelug school; monastic chanting there is commonly in Tibetan, and the Dalai Lamas are revered.

games.q: you're Altan Khan. a Tibetan teacher whose name means ocean has moved you deeply. how do you honor him?
o: give him gold and send him home.
give him a title meaning ocean, in your own language.
ask him to become your general.
games.why: the Khan named him Dalai, ocean in Mongolian, echoing his Tibetan name, Gyatso.

practice: Picture today's Mongolia, between Russia to the north and China to the south, with no coast at all; Altan Khan's own lands lay just south of it, in what is now China.

A people far from any sea gave a line of teachers its word for ocean. With each breath, picture the grasslands rolling out wide in every direction, like water, and let the mind be that wide for a while.

wordCard.voice: Mongolia. The land of the Mongols, whose ruler Altan Khan gave Sonam Gyatso the title Dalai, ocean, and where the teaching put down deep roots.

carryVoice: Your line: the ocean of wisdom. Two languages, one name, said twice in thanks. That's day nine hundred forty-one.
